A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HAMLET and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. The retained material can be matched reliably despite the expanded appendix and relocated displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original real-robot evaluations, simulation experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in Sections 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds initialization comparisons, a longer-horizon task evaluation, and experiments applying HAMLET to autoregressive VLAs.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same moment tokens, TCL objective, causal Transformer memory module, and action conditioning, including Equations 1–7. The autoregressive evaluations do not specify a distinct algorithmic adaptation; Appendix A.3 provides additional implementation details for the retained design.

E1.justification: V3 retains the original tasks and simulation benchmarks and adds Pick-and-Place Three Times (Table 13). This scenario requires tracking three completed operations and returning to the ready position, testing a longer temporal dependency within the existing manipulation domain. Testing additional backbones does not add dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained policy baselines, Tables 10–11 introduce comparisons against SimCLR, single-view TCN, and multi-view TCN, substantially expanding evaluation of the initialization design. OpenVLA also becomes an evaluated LIBERO comparator in Table 14; v1 includes only its reported SimplerEnv scores.

E3.justification: New autoregressive experiments introduce separate per-suite LIBERO training for OpenVLA, unlike the retained joint-suite experiment, and batch sizes of 32 for OpenVLA and 64 for π0-FAST. Table 13 adds average executed pick-and-place operations alongside success over 24 trials. Existing experiments retain their stated protocols.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends v1's component ablations with alternative contrastive initialization designs (Tables 10–11), TCL-removal analyses across demonstration budgets and LIBERO (Table 12), and a task testing dependencies beyond the default four-step memory window (Table 13). Table 8 also extends resource-cost analysis to CogACT. Existing qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. V3 retains point-estimate reporting and the same descriptive frame-count statistics in Table 7. The added task follows the existing 24-trial reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 8 and 11–14 add resource measurements, initialization and TCL-ablation results, and new task/backbone comparisons. Examples include GR00T N1.5 versus HAMLET at 8.3% versus 37.5% on Pick-and-Place Three Times, and OpenVLA versus HAMLET at 48.6% versus 57.6% on LIBERO-Long. These are newly reported comparisons. Table 2 also changes HAMLET's LIBERO average from 97.7% to 97.6% without changing its suite scores, although new Table 11 still reports 97.7%.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–7 are unchanged, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. V3's account of information persisting through successive KV-cache entries is an informal mechanism explanation rather than a formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adapting pretrained VLAs through moment tokens and lightweight memory to improve history-dependent control efficiently. The new appendix experiments support the existing backbone-generality claim. The small LIBERO numerical correction does not redefine the core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds causal confusion from spurious temporal correlations as an explanation for multi-frame failures. Appendix B.1 adds a KV-cache explanation for performance beyond the explicit memory window and interprets autoregressive results as evidence of architectural generality. Appendix C nevertheless retains the earlier warning that autoregressive applicability may be limited.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies augmentation details, uniform within-trajectory negative sampling more than 16 timesteps apart, and a contrastive temperature of 0.07. V1's main text already mentions blur, noise, and occlusion, so these details do not establish a changed procedure. V3 also adds parameter counts, resource information, and batch sizes and repository references for the autoregressive experiments.

R1.justification: V3 expands discussion of robot memory and causal confusion through works including Wen et al., Seo et al., Huang et al., and De Haan et al., and adds SimCLR for the initialization comparisons. The central positioning—augmenting pretrained VLAs instead of training memory policies from scratch—remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact. V3 makes localized wording changes, including replacing some 'plug-and-play' descriptions with 'easily integrable,' expands related-work and appendix explanations, and updates author, affiliation, publication-header, and acknowledgment text. There is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V3 adds substantial tabular presentation through six tables: resource costs, pair-construction designs, initialization comparisons, expanded TCL ablations, longer-horizon results, and autoregressive results (Tables 8 and 10–14). V1's detailed RoboCasa Table 8 becomes Table 9. All thirteen figures retain their content, while Figures 8–9 are relocated together and Table 4 moves.

improvement.justification: The added initialization controls, longer-horizon test, and autoregressive evaluations strengthen evidence for claims previously supported more narrowly, while Appendix A.3 improves reproducibility. These gains are partly offset by incomplete integration: Appendix C retains an autoregressive-applicability caveat despite Table 14, and Table 11 conflicts with Tables 2 and 12 on the LIBERO average. The revision provides a clear but limited net quality improvement.
